extracted.intended_audience: students of algebraic topology (advanced undergraduates / beginning graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook section developing singular homology: definitions (chains, cycles, boundaries), functoriality, homotopy invariance, reduced and relative homology, long exact sequences, excision, and barycentric subdivision with proofs and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition by path-components (Proposition 2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding to the decomposition of a space X into its path-components X_α there is an isomorphism H_n(X) ≈ ⊕_α H_n(X_α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: singular simplices have path-connected images so C_n(X) splits as direct sum of C_n(X_α); boundary maps preserve decomposition, so Ker ∂ and Im ∂ split and hence homology splits. Use when computing homology of disconnected spaces: compute each component separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: H_0 for path-connected spaces (Proposition 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is nonempty and path-connected, then H_0(X) ≈ Z. For any X, H_0(X) is a direct sum of Z's, one for each path-component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augmentation map ε: C_0(X)→Z (ε(∑ n_i σ_i) = ∑ n_i) is surjective when X nonempty; show Ker ε = Im ∂_1 when X path-connected by constructing paths from a basepoint to vertices to show 0-chains of total coefficient 0 are boundaries. Use to identify H_0 as counting components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology of a point (Proposition 2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a point, then H_n(X) = 0 for n > 0 and H_0(X) ≈ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chain complex has unique singular simplex σ_n for each n and boundaries alternate between 0 and isomorphisms, yielding trivial homology except H_0 ≈ Z. Use as base case for many computations and for reduced homology conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced homology (augmentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced homology H̃_n(X) is defined from the augmented chain complex ... → C_1(X) → C_0(X) →^ε Z → 0; for nonempty X, H̃_n(X) ≈ H_n(X) for n > 0 and H_0(X) ≈ H̃_0(X) ⊕ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require X nonempty to avoid homology in dimension −1. Think of the extra Z as generated by the unique map from the empty simplex. Use reduced homology when one wants a point to have trivial homology in all dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced chain maps and functoriality (Proposition 2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f: X→Y induces chain maps f_♯ : C_n(X)→C_n(Y) by composition; these satisfy f_♯ ∂ = ∂ f_♯ and therefore induce homomorphisms f_* : H_n(X)→H_n(Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: (f∘g)_* = f_* g_* and identity induces identity on homology. This is the basic functoriality of homology and is used whenever mapping spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy invariance of induced maps (Theorem 2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two maps f, g : X→Y are homotopic, then they induce the same homomorphism f_* = g_* : H_n(X)→H_n(Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses prism operators P : C_n(X)→C_{n+1}(Y) constructed from a homotopy F and the relation ∂P = g_♯ − f_♯ − P∂, showing g_♯(α) − f_♯(α) is a boundary for cycles α. Use to show homotopy equivalent spaces have isomorphic homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy equivalence implies isomorphism on homology (Corollary 2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f : X→Y is a homotopy equivalence, then the induced maps f_* : H_n(X)→H_n(Y) are isomorphisms for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows formally from functoriality and homotopy invariance. In particular, contractible spaces have trivial homology in all positive dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-homotopic chain maps induce same homomorphism (Proposition 2.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chain-homotopic chain maps induce the same homomorphism on homology: if P is a chain homotopy between f_♯ and g_♯, then f_* = g_*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic analogue of homotopy invariance; used when constructing chain homotopies like prism operators or subdivision homotopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence ... → A_{n+1} →^{α_{n+1}} A_n →^{α_n} A_{n-1} → ... is exact if Ker α_n = Im α_{n+1} for each n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently α_n α_{n+1} = 0 and the homology groups of the associated chain complex are trivial. Short exact sequences 0→A→B→C→0 encode injections, surjections, and quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence for a good pair (Theorem 2.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a space and A is a nonempty closed subspace that is a deformation retract of some neighborhood in X (a 'good pair'), then there is a long exact sequence ... → H_n(A) →^{i_*} H_n(X) →^{j_*} H_n(X/A) →^{∂} H_{n-1}(A) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here i is inclusion A ↪ X and j is the quotient X→X/A. The boundary ∂ is constructed algebraically via short exact sequences of chain complexes. For CW complexes and subcomplex A, (X,A) is a good pair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pair criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A pair (X, A) is a 'good pair' if A is a nonempty closed subspace that is a deformation retract of some neighborhood in X (e.g., a subcomplex of a CW complex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good pair hypothesis ensures that H_n(X/A) can be used and the long exact sequence for (X,A) holds with X/A replacing relative homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of homology of spheres (Corollary 2.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: H_n(S^n) ≈ Z and H_i(S^n) = 0 for i ≠ n (for n > 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute using pair (D^n, S^{n-1}) where D^n is contractible so appropriate maps in the long exact sequence are isomorphisms; proceed by induction starting at S^0.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retraction of disk boundary; Brouwer fixed point (Corollary 2.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: ∂D^n is not a retract of D^n. Hence every continuous f: D^n → D^n has a fixed point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If r: D^n → ∂D^n were a retraction, induced maps on homology would give a contradiction (map would have to be both identity and zero on H_{n-1}(∂D^n) ≈ Z). This yields Brouwer's fixed point theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of relative homology H_n(X,A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A ⊂ X, C_n(X,A) := C_n(X)/C_n(A) with induced boundary maps; H_n(X,A) = Ker ∂ / Im ∂ (homology of this quotient complex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements of H_n(X,A) are represented by relative cycles α ∈ C_n(X) with ∂α ∈ C_{n-1}(A); α is trivial iff α = ∂β + γ for some β ∈ C_{n+1}(X), γ ∈ C_n(A). Intuitively 'homology of X modulo A'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of a pair (algebraic Theorem 2.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence of chain complexes 0→A→B→C→0 induces a long exact sequence ... → H_n(A) → H_n(B) → H_n(C) →^{∂} H_{n-1}(A) → ... on homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boundary ∂ constructed by lifting cycles and taking boundaries; proof checks six exactness conditions (Im i_* ⊂ Ker j_*, Im j_* ⊂ Ker ∂, Im ∂ ⊂ Ker i_*, and converses). This is the algebraic engine behind topological long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary map description in topology
rubrics_metrics.description: In topological long exact sequence for (X,A), the boundary ∂ : H_n(X,A) → H_{n-1}(A) sends a class [α] (represented by relative cycle α) to the class of ∂α in H_{n-1}(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is immediate from the algebraic construction of the boundary homomorphism. Useful for computing connecting homomorphisms explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative functoriality and homotopy invariance for pairs (Proposition 2.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map of pairs f : (X,A) → (Y,B) (i.e., f(A) ⊂ B) induces f_♯ : C_n(X,A) → C_n(Y,B) and hence f_* : H_n(X,A) → H_n(Y,B); homotopic maps of pairs induce the same map on relative homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof adapts prism operator to relative setting: prism operator takes C_n(A) to C_{n+1}(B) so descends to quotient. Use to get homotopy invariance for relative groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of a triple
rubrics_metrics.description: For B ⊂ A ⊂ X there is a long exact sequence ... → H_n(A,B) → H_n(X,B) → H_n(X,A) → H_{n-1}(A,B) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the long exact sequence associated to the short exact sequence 0→C_n(A,B)→C_n(X,B)→C_n(X,A)→0. Special case with B a point recovers reduced pair sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision theorem (Theorem 2.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Z ⊂ A ⊂ X with cl(Z) ⊂ int(A), the inclusion (X−Z, A−Z) ↪ (X,A) induces isomorphisms H_n(X−Z, A−Z) → H_n(X,A) for all n. Equivalently, if A,B ⊂ X have interiors covering X then inclusion (B, A∩B) ↪ (X,A) induces H_n(B, A∩B) → H_n(X,A) isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation between versions: set B = X−Z. Excision is proved via barycentric subdivision allowing chains to be made arbitrarily small so they lie in cover elements; key technical tool for computing relative homology by localizing computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup of chains subordinate to a cover (definition before Prop 2.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open cover U = {U_j} of X, C_n^U(X) is the subgroup of C_n(X) consisting of chains ∑ n_i σ_i such that each σ_i has image contained in some set of the cover U; these form a chain complex with induced boundary maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce homology computations to chains subordinate to a cover; central in the barycentric subdivision proof of excision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain homotopy equivalence of subordinate chains (Proposition 2.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion ι: C_n^U(X) ↪ C_n(X) is a chain homotopy equivalence: there exists a chain map ρ: C_n(X) → C_n^U(X) with ιρ and ρι chain-homotopic to the identity; hence ι induces isomorphisms H_n^U(X) ≈ H_n(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct ρ via iterated barycentric subdivision S and a chain homotopy D built from T and S. Key step for excision: make simplices small enough that their images lie in single cover elements; ρ and the homotopy are explicit (S, T, D constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Barycentric subdivision diameter bound
rubrics_metrics.description: In barycentric subdivision of an n-simplex [v_0,...,v_n], the diameter of each subdivided simplex is at most n/(n+1) times the diameter of the original simplex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: repeated barycentric subdivision shrinks diameters to 0 (factor tends to 0 as iterate r→∞). Important because bound does not depend on simplex shape, enabling control over sizes of singular simplices in arbitrary metric ambient spaces and use of Lebesgue numbers for covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision operator S and chain homotopy T (construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a subdivision operator S: C_n(X)→C_n(X) (barycentric subdivision on chains) satisfying ∂S = S∂, and a chain homotopy T: C_n(X)→C_{n+1}(X) with ∂T + T∂ = id − S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction proceeds via linear chains and cone operators on barycenters, then extends to singular chains by naturality (σ_♯). These provide explicit chain homotopies showing S is chain-homotopic to the identity; used to construct ρ and prove Proposition 2.21 and excision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated subdivision homotopy (Dm)
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator D_m = Σ_{0≤i<m} T S^i gives a chain homotopy between id and S^m, since ∂D_m + D_m∂ = id − S^m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose m large so S^m(σ) has small diameter (lies in a single cover set). Use D_m and variable m(σ) to define global D and ρ = id − ∂D − D∂ mapping into subordinate chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision proof scheme using subdivision and quotienting
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove excision for a decomposition X=A∪B, use cover U={A,B} and show inclusion C_n(B)/C_n(A∩B) → C_n(X)/C_n(A) induces homology isomorphism by constructing ρ and chain homotopies that respect A and B so descend to quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All maps in the barycentric subdivision homotopy take chains in A to chains in A, hence descend to quotient complexes; combined with isomorphism of quotient chain groups yields H_n(B,A∩B) ≈ H_n(X,A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient to suspension/quotient space isomorphism for good pairs (Proposition 2.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: For good pairs (X,A), the quotient map q: (X,A) → (X/A, A/A) induces isomorphisms q_* : H_n(X,A) → H_n(X/A, A/A) ≈ H_n(X/A) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neighborhood deformation retraction to A and excision to replace (X,A) by (X/A, A/A); this allows passing from relative homology to homology of quotient spaces in computations (e.g., produce S^n as D^n/∂D^n).
